cohorts.subjects: Dry bone: complete sets of lumbar vertebrae of adult Nigerians from the osteological collection of the Department of Anatomy, University of Ibadan, Nigeria (measured by the author of the University of Ilorin). Full medical histories were not available for all; persons who died of chronic skeletal disorders or related causes were left out as far as possible, and specimens with osteophytes or other evidence of bone disease were excluded. Ethnic group within Nigeria not stated; the author counts the sample among black populations (p. 74). How sex and age were known is not stated. In Table 3 these are the 'Present study' columns.
cohorts.n_units: 122 complete sets of lumbar vertebrae (79 male, 43 female; the total is the sum, not printed), L1 to L5; per-level n not printed (Inference: 610 vertebrae if no set lacked one)
cohorts.ages: 23 to 60 years (whole sample; not given by sex)
cohorts.page: p. 69 (PDF 1), p. 71 (PDF 3); n repeated in Table 3, p. 73 (PDF 5)

techniques.instrument: sliding Vernier caliper, read to the nearest 0.1 mm
techniques.how: Direct measurement of each isolated dry lumbar vertebra. Canal midsagittal diameter: in the midline from the back of the body to the deep surface of the posterior wall, at the narrowest point near the upper border, opposite a slight anterior bulge of the posterior wall (Fig. 1a, i). Body AP diameter: in the midline (Fig. 1a, ii), called the maximum AP diameter but taken at mid-waist where the body is narrowest. Inferior vertebral notch AP diameter: the greatest horizontal distance from the back of the lower part of the body to the deep surface of the lamina (Fig. 1b, N); side not stated. Canal shape, nerve groove and foramen shape were also noted but not reported. Tables 4 and 6 give ratios of the group means; Table 2 gives 95% limits of normal by Bradford Hill's formula.
techniques.magnification: not applicable: direct caliper measurement on dry bone, no imaging
techniques.observers: not stated (Inference: the author alone); no repeat or second-reader figure reported

within_paper: One set of subjects: the canal, body AP and inferior notch were all measured on the same 122 dry lumbar sets (p. 71-72, PDF 3-4). Table 2 is derived from Table 1 (mean +/- 2 SD), Table 3's 'Present study' columns and Table 4's canal columns repeat Table 1's means, Table 6 repeats Table 5's notch means and Table 4's body AP means (with male notch L3/L4 swapped and male L5 body 34.2 against 32.2). The Zulu and Sotho columns of Table 3 are Eisenstein's separate subjects, not measured here (p. 73-74, PDF 5-6).
